answer: The attacker pays in compute, time, and reputation every time an alias is slashed, and these costs grow faster than the influence the cluster gains, making a large coordinated farm economically self-defeating. It resists because the per-account limit caps any single farm, spreading the surplus across many passing identities instead of letting one cluster monopolize it. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.
